title: Hierarchical tenant fencing and noise containment
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: provide a multi-layer GPU fleet partitioning system that enforces tenant separation while minimizing waste and maintaining throughput guarantees for Dedicated customers. Deliverables include node-label driven hard fencing, tenant-specific soft-eviction windows, per-tenant circuit breakers, and a noise detector that feeds autoscaler and quota subsystems. This work ties scheduling, runtime eviction, and the autoscaler so we can meet burst guarantees without cross-tenant interference. Constraints: must work with existing CUDA/NCCL-enabled pools, support both MIG and whole-GPU profiles, and integrate with Dedicated autoscaling policies without requiring customers to change their runtime configs. Prioritizes correctness and observability over micro-optimizations in initial rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Node labeling system implemented and retrofittable via fleet agent
Per-tenant hard fencing enforced in scheduler with test coverage across MIG/whole-GPU nodes
Noisy neighbor detector alerts with precision >= 90% on synthetic workloads
Soft eviction windows and tenant circuit breakers reduce cross-tenant latency spikes by >= 70% in bench tests
End-to-end e2e test demonstrating autoscaler respecting tenant caps under load
tech_decisions: Use node labels + grpc admission controller for hard fencing instead of rewriting scheduler core to reduce blast radius
Implement noisy neighbor detection as a streaming aggregator using existing runtime telemetry (token latency distribution + GPU SM utilization) to avoid a separate agent process
Adopt a two-tier quota enforcement: immediate cgroup-based soft throttles + periodic hard eviction wave to reclaim resources
Make eviction windows configurable per project via console, default conservative values in release

2025-09-25: Design review feedback: add per-tenant circuit breaker metrics and expose in Console; action item to add telemetry endpoints

2025-10-01: Integration spike: autoscaler honored soft quota under synthetic burst test but hard eviction still triggers earlier than expected; root cause: eviction scoring did not account for KV cache hot prefixes
2025-10-03: Mitigation: adjusted eviction score to penalize small-KV-cache-hit tenants less; added follow-up ENG-60300 for KV cache-aware eviction refinement
test_plan: Unit tests for admission controller (node label permutations)
Staging e2e: mix of 10 tenants with MIG/whole-GPU profiles, ramped synthetic traffic to validate eviction windows
Chaos test: randomly kill GPU nodes while running noisy neighbor scenarios to validate graceful reassignment and quota enforcement
Load test: verify autoscaler does not overshoot reserved capacity under bursty workloads
rollout_plan: Canary: enable fencing on 2 Dedicated clusters for internal teams only
Expand: gradual enablement by org with monitoring dashboards and rollback flag
GA: on-by-default for new Dedicated customers; migration guide for existing customers to opt-in or pin nodes
notes: Trade-offs considered: planned hard partitioning reduces bin-packing efficiency but provides stronger SLAs; we chose hierarchical fencing to allow mixed mode (soft+hard) per customer tier
Open question: whether to surface tenant eviction score in Console or keep it infra-only; PM leaning toward surfacing a normalized score for transparency
feedback: PM review 2025-09-25: move default soft eviction window from 60s to 120s to reduce churn
SRE review 2025-09-27: require a kill-switch that disables soft eviction globally for emergency incidents
